tagline: Into Hertford on an S-shaped bridge that still swings.
intro: US 17 Business leaves the main highway north of Hertford and takes two miles to rejoin it. Near Winfall it crosses Mill Creek, then sweeps down over the Perquimans River into Hertford, an early colonial port of entry and the county seat since 1758. The river runs on about ten miles southeast into Albemarle Sound.

Hertford lived on lumber through the first part of the 20th century. The state guidebook notes that the county courthouse holds records from the late 1600s, among them the Durant Deed, the oldest deed on record in North Carolina.

moments.title: Mill Creek
moments.text: Named Vosses Creek for the family that owned the land before 1700, it had become Brights Mill Creek by the end of the 19th century, after the local mill owner.

moments.title: S Swing Bridge
moments.text: The road enters Hertford on a swing bridge with S-shaped approaches, believed the only working one of its kind, where an earlier floating bridge was simply unhooked and let drift aside for boats.

moments.title: Newbold-White House
moments.text: A mile and a half on down Church Street stands a Quaker's brick house dated by its timbers to 1730, the oldest known brick building in the state, later used for court sessions.
